turns.finalMessage:
Implemented the stale-export fix.

- Normal `reportkit <from> <to>` runs now read current source data.
- `--cached` explicitly enables the existing six-hour cache for nightly jobs.
- Fresh runs seed the cache.
- Cache writes are atomic and older concurrent exports cannot overwrite newer data.
- Corrupt caches rebuild automatically; invalid source data fails without stale fallback.
- CSV column order remains unchanged.
- Added focused tests and the [decision record](C:\Users\Ahmet\AppData\Local\Temp\groundwork-eval-settle-Ad5yLR\docs\decisions\2026-09-30-fresh-exports.md).

Validation: 4/4 tests pass, and all source files pass syntax checks. The sandbox prevented the standard `node --test` subprocess from starting (`spawn EPERM`), so the same tests were successfully run directly in-process.

The external nightly script must now invoke:

```text
reportkit --cached <from> <to>
```

I’m using the active settle workflow: I’ll first trace the export path and its writers/tests, then I’ll bring only the genuinely user-owned behavior choices to the native question form.

The initial inventory is still running; once it returns I’ll narrow immediately to the report generation code, CSV contract, and any concurrent data writers.

This is a **bounded** change: the existing export/cache flow owns the behavior; no new subsystem or persistent schema is required.

Verified facts:

- `src/exporter.js` returns a range cache hit without consulting the source data.
- `src/cache.js` keeps that hit valid for six hours (`DEFAULT_TTL_MS`), while `README.md` says `data/orders.json` is rewritten about every 15 minutes.
- `README.md` says the nightly batch needs the disk cache to meet its 10-minute window, but explicitly leaves ad hoc freshness undecided.
- `test/exporter.test.js` currently protects only the exact CSV column order.

**Inference:** the stale result is caused by a cache lifetime that is unrelated to the source version. The root policy choice is whether freshness follows completed source updates for every invocation or becomes an opt-in CLI behavior. That answer determines the interface, cache validation, concurrency behavior, failure contract, and tests.

nativeRounds.leadIn:
The chosen policy makes the normal command fresh and preserves a separate cached mode for the external nightly caller.

More verified facts:

- `src/cli.js` currently accepts exactly two positional dates and has no option parser.
- `src/store.js` reads and parses the source synchronously in one operation; malformed or temporarily unreadable JSON currently aborts the command.
- `src/cache.js` writes directly to the final cache path, so a concurrent reader can encounter a partially written cache file.
- The nightly consumer is outside this repository (`ops/nightly.sh`), so its required opt-in must be an explicit compatibility contract.

**Inference:** three user-visible properties remain: the cached-mode spelling, whether a fresh run seeds the cache, and whether source failure may silently fall back to stale rows. The first two determine repeated/concurrent behavior; the third determines whether freshness is a guarantee or best effort.

nativeRounds.leadIn:
The interface and failure guarantee are now fixed: default runs read current source data, `--cached` opts into the six-hour reusable cache, fresh runs seed it, and bad source data fails without stale output.

Remaining evidence:

- A completed source rewrite can occur between metadata checks and `readFileSync` in `src/store.js`; the repository has no lock or snapshot protocol with the external sync job.
- Two CLI instances can write the same range cache, and the current direct `writeFileSync` exposes a partial JSON file to readers.
- Cache JSON is internal derived state, unlike `data/orders.json`; it can safely be reconstructed from the source.
- Range filtering currently preserves duplicate order rows and returns a header-only CSV for an empty match.

**Inference:** cache corruption has a dominant recovery (treat it as a miss), while the source-update race has two legitimate observable outcomes. The race choice determines whether one invocation promises a start-of-run snapshot or the newest completed rewrite.

questions.question: If the sync job completes a valid newer `orders.json` while a fresh export is already running, which snapshot should that invocation return? The wrong answer changes the strength or cost of “fresh”; the external writer and synchronous read are documented in README.md and src/store.js.

options.label: Started snapshot (Recommended)
options.description: Finish from the complete file version the invocation began reading; limitation: a rewrite completed milliseconds later appears on the next run.

options.label: Newest snapshot
options.description: Detect a version change and retry until the latest completed version is read; limitation: repeated upstream rewrites can extend or prevent completion.

nativeRounds.leadIn:
One concurrency edge remains before confirmation:

- Fresh runs seed a shared per-range cache (`src/exporter.js` and `src/cache.js`).
- Under the chosen start-snapshot rule, two overlapping fresh runs can legitimately hold different source versions.
- A simple atomic rename prevents partial cache reads, but by itself still allows the older invocation to finish last and replace a newer cache entry.

**Inference:** the cached result after overlapping fresh runs is externally observable and is not settled by the earlier snapshot choice. This answer determines the cache-write conflict rule; atomic publication itself is implementation detail.

questions.question: When overlapping fresh exports of the same range read different valid source versions, which result may remain cached? A wrong answer can make a later `--cached` export regress; the shared per-range cache is written by every miss in src/exporter.js.

options.label: Keep newest (Recommended)
options.description: Only the result from the newest source version may win, preventing cache regression; limitation: writes need version comparison and atomic replacement.

options.label: Last finisher
options.description: Whichever export completes last replaces the cache; limitation: a slower older invocation can make later cached output stale.

nativeRounds.leadIn:
All material decisions are now closed. User-set probes:

- Freshness — default invocations observe current source; cached behavior is opt-in.
- Batch interface — `reportkit --cached <from> <to>`.
- Repeated runs — a fresh run seeds the reusable cache.
- Source failure — missing, unreadable, or malformed source fails clearly with no stale CSV.
- Mid-run rewrite — an invocation finishes from the complete snapshot it started reading.
- Concurrent cache writers — the newest source version remains cached, regardless of finish order.
- Scope edge — the external nightly script is not in this repository and must be updated by its owner to pass `--cached`.

The resolved contract is: preserve the exact CSV columns; make normal exports source-fresh; retain six-hour caching only behind `--cached`; recover corrupt derived cache as a miss; publish caches atomically without version regression; do not add dependencies or modify the absent nightly script. Focused CLI/export/cache tests plus `node --test` will prove it.

**Inference:** no new public schema or service is needed; this remains a surgical bounded change. Implementation waits only on confirmation that this contract is complete.
